title: Simulate CommonJS Module Cache & require()
subtopicTitle: Module Systems: ESM vs CommonJS & Circular Dependencies
problemStatement: Implement `createModuleEnvironment()` that exposes `defineModule(id, fn)` and `require(id)`. Modules must only be evaluated once; subsequent `require` calls must return the cached `module.exports` object.
interviewTrap: Forgetting to populate cache.set(id, mod) BEFORE calling the module factory causes infinite recursion on circular dependencies.

testCases.name: Exports and requires a module successfully
testCases.testFn: const env = createModuleEnvironment(); env.defineModule('math', (exports) => { exports.add = (a, b) => a + b; }); return env.require('math').add(2, 3);

testCases.name: Subsequent requires return cached instance without re-evaluating
testCases.input: verify factory is only invoked once
testCases.testFn: const env = createModuleEnvironment(); let calls = 0; env.defineModule('counter', (exports) => { calls++; exports.val = 42; }); env.require('counter'); env.require('counter'); return calls;

testCases.name: Throws descriptive error on unknown module ID
testCases.testFn: const env = createModuleEnvironment(); try { env.require('unknown'); return 'no-error'; } catch (e) { return e.message; }

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: CommonJS exports are evaluated at runtime and copied by value into a module.exports object. ESM exports are live references bound during static analysis, meaning changes in the exporter reflect immediately in the importer.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for CommonJS module.exports & require cache mechanics.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), CommonJS module.exports & require cache mechanics is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
